# Taylor's solved AMM policy in Solidity: Gaussian filter + qm tables, confirmed on the real engine

Goal: port Taylor's (gtmcknight) solved policy from `github.com/gtmcknight/amm-sim` at commit `4812a6382311624e1506aca131ca35c378f930d9`, folder `research/solved`, into a `contract Strategy is AMMStrategyBase` for paradigm.xyz/puzzles/amm that beats our file t03 on the real engine, within 24,576 runtime bytes, an afterSwap peak of at most 245,000 gas and zero OutOfGas, with the tables compressed and gates P, Q and F passed.

All policy credit is Taylor's (gtmcknight): the dynamic program, the Gaussian filter (`real.py`), the plain and qm tables and the replica. Every contract below says so in its header.

No trunk repository was created for this goal (`goal.json` reports `trunk: null`): every piece of code lives inside the result artifacts, which are public at `https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/<sha256 of the result.md>`. The artifact ids used below are listed in section 9.

## 1. The best contract: qt1 (`TaylorGaussianQMSpline`)

qt1 is Taylor's Gaussian filter (port-3's filter, in trim-2's three-slot shell) quoting from Taylor's qm tables, compressed by qm-spline into 10,167 bytes of cubic B-spline coefficients and decoded at runtime. It is the contract the requester submitted after this goal's round 5: it sits on the board at 524.9403, 8th place (requester note 8), up from trim-1's 524.1189 and port-3's 523.3369, with IB at 522.00. The board gain over trim-1 (+0.82) matches the local measurement.

### 1.1 Paired gain on fresh engine seeds

Every engine figure in this report comes from the pinned protocol: amm-challenge at `6b6921f8d463314aa7c96234e1be25a25245f704`, each strategy alone against the 30 bps VanillaStrategy through `amm_sim_rs.run_batch(X, VanillaStrategy, configs, 8)`, configs per `MatchRunner._build_configs` with `default_rng(seed)` drawing size, rate and sigma, score = `edges["submission"]`, differences paired by seed, se = sample sd / sqrt(n). Seeds were taken fresh from 9500000 upward and never reused (registry in section 8).

qt1's own run (seeds 9535000..9535127, n=128):

| Pair | n | mean_diff | se | wins | worst5 (seed, diff) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| qt1 minus t03 | 128 | **+2.160** | 0.110 | 125/128 | (9535096, -0.879), (9535060, -0.291), (9535073, -0.160), (9535100, +0.004), (9535078, +0.239) |
| qt1 minus trim-2 | 128 | **+0.819** | 0.055 | 117/128 | (9535096, -0.683), (9535125, -0.500), (9535054, -0.366), (9535055, -0.289), (9535052, -0.202) |
| trim-2 minus t03 (same seeds) | 128 | +1.341 | 0.117 | 111/128 | (9535060, -1.637), (9535064, -1.478), (9535016, -1.331), (9535057, -0.886), (9535100, -0.777) |

IB was not run on qt1's block. By offset through t03 (t03 minus IB is +0.78 se 0.02 on the 1,792 qm confirmation seeds and +0.745 se 0.084 on the r1-baseline block), qt1 is about +2.9 over IB.

The policy qt1 implements (Gaussian filter + qm-spline tables, fees within 5.83e-6 bps of the same Python reference) was confirmed on 1,792 fresh seeds through qm-2, a sibling contract with the same tables and the same reference (section 2). Pooled over its seven handed blocks (seeds 9613312..9613823 and 9614080..9615359, every seed once per arm, recomputed here from the per-seed CSVs):

| qm policy (qm-2) minus | n | mean_diff | se | wins | worst5 (seed, diff) | best5 (seed, diff) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| trim-1 (board 524.1189) | 1,792 | **+0.8755** | 0.0158 | 1,625 | (9613816, -1.250), (9614759, -1.108), (9613349, -1.024), (9615035, -1.009), (9614347, -0.923) | (9613711, +4.221), (9613335, +3.260), (9614302, +2.784), (9614411, +2.766), (9614490, +2.703) |
| t03 | 1,792 | **+2.2724** | 0.0304 | 1,751 | (9613399, -2.487), (9613493, -2.407), (9613540, -2.042), (9614831, -1.594), (9614809, -1.330) | (9614955, +7.098), (9613468, +7.091), (9614327, +6.752), (9614199, +6.542), (9615278, +6.302) |
| IB | 1,792 | **+3.0539** | 0.0340 | 1,785 | (9613493, -1.605), (9613399, -0.795), (9614598, -0.197), (9613672, -0.187), (9613540, -0.125) | (9614349, +14.934), (9614140, +13.979), (9614199, +9.013), (9614203, +8.353), (9614327, +8.240) |

Two things to keep straight about that transfer. First, qm-2 and qt1 were never compared callback by callback: both match the same Python reference (filter + `real.py` qm rule over the decoded qm-spline tables) to a maximum of 5.826e-06 bps, qm-2 in trim-1's shell and qt1 in trim-2's, so the two contracts differ in fixed-point rounding at or below that level, not in policy. Second, qm-2 ran out of gas on 33 of 19.5 million callbacks in those blocks (section 2.2); an OutOfGas callback leaves the previous fees in force for one step, which can only have cost qm-2 score, so the pooled figures are a slight understatement of what a gas-safe contract with the same fees scores. The eighth block (qa3, seeds 9613824..9614079) was still running when this write-up was made, so n is 1,792, not 2,048.

Against the requester's successive bars: qt1 clears ">= +0.3 over t03", ">= +0.3 over port-3" and ">= +0.3 over trim-1" on 1,792 seeds with se 0.016. Nothing in this goal clears the last bar set in note 8 (">= +0.3 over qt1"): the only candidates measured after qt1 are the same policy in other shells (section 3), which are its equals by construction.

### 1.2 Complete Strategy.sol of qt1

Extract exactly the block below, including its final newline; its SHA-256 is `c68887cff61180e12ba2b1ceb333edf76a830f91f63b5d775a8806fb9ec08aca`. It imports only the two base files of the pinned challenge and needs no payload, library, assembly or external call at runtime.

```solidity
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity ^0.8.24;
import {AMMStrategyBase} from "./AMMStrategyBase.sol";
import {TradeInfo} from "./IAMMStrategy.sol";
// Solved AMM policy by Taylor (gtmcknight), amm-sim 4812a638 research/solved: Gaussian filter + qm tables (qm_k1e-5.json),
// fee rule of real.py's qm variant (sd level, phase, synced flag). All credit for the policy, filter and tables: Taylor.
// Tables compressed by qm-spline (cubic B-splines, QMS1 blob sha256 3ac7cb88...); filter, 3-slot state, math and fee conversion
// from trim-2 (port-3's filter); synced flag stored in bit 255 of slot 2.
// Taylor source: https://github.com/gtmcknight/amm-sim/tree/4812a6382311624e1506aca131ca35c378f930d9/research/solved
contract Strategy is AMMStrategyBase {
    int256 constant U=1e18;
    int256 constant LN2=693147180559945309;
    uint256 constant M64=0xffffffffffffffff;
    // slots[0] = m (int128) | v (int128)<<128 ; slots[1] = sp (int128) | r (int128)<<128 ; slots[2] = fb | fa<<64 | t<<128 | cnt<<192
    function getName() external pure override returns(string memory) { unchecked {return "TaylorGaussianQMSpline";} }
    function mul(int256 a,int256 b) internal pure returns(int256){ unchecked {return a*b/U;} }
    function divi(int256 a,int256 b) internal pure returns(int256){ unchecked {return a*U/b;} }
    function ab(int256 x) internal pure returns(int256){ unchecked {return x<0?-x:x;} }
    function clip(int256 x,int256 a,int256 b) internal pure returns(int256){ unchecked {return x<a?a:(x>b?b:x);} }
    function ln(int256 x) internal pure returns(int256 z){ unchecked {
        require(x>0); int256 k;
        while(x< U){x*=2;k--;}
        while(x>=2*U){x/=2;k++;}
        int256 y=divi(x-U,x+U); int256 y2=mul(y,y); int256 q=y; z=y;
        for(int256 n=3;n<=29;n+=2){q=mul(q,y2);z+=q/n;}
        return 2*z+k*LN2;
    } }
    function exp(int256 x) internal pure returns(int256){ unchecked {
        if(x< -42*U)return 0; require(x<60*U);
        int256 k=(x>=0?x+LN2/2:x-LN2/2)/LN2; int256 r=x-k*LN2;
        int256 r2=mul(r,r);
        int256 even=665280*U+mul(r2,75600*U+mul(r2,840*U+r2));
        int256 odd=mul(r,332640*U+mul(r2,10080*U+mul(r2,42*U)));
        int256 s=divi(even+odd,even-odd);
        return k>=0?s*int256(uint256(1)<<uint256(k)):s/int256(uint256(1)<<uint256(-k));
    } }
    function root(int256 x) internal pure returns(int256){ unchecked {
        if(x<=0)return 0; uint256 n=uint256(x)*1e18;uint256 z=n;uint256 r=1;
        if(z>>128>0){z>>=128;r<<=64;} if(z>>64>0){z>>=64;r<<=32;}
        if(z>>32>0){z>>=32;r<<=16;} if(z>>16>0){z>>=16;r<<=8;}
        if(z>>8>0){z>>=8;r<<=4;} if(z>>4>0){z>>=4;r<<=2;} if(z>>2>0){r<<=1;}
        for(uint256 i=0;i<7;i++)r=(r+n/r)/2;
        return int256(r<n/r?r:n/r);
    } }
    function pdf(int256 x) internal pure returns(int256){ unchecked {if(ab(x)>10*U)return 0;return divi(exp(-mul(x,x)/2),2506628274631000200);} }
    // Hart rational normal tail approximation; erf(x)=2*Phi(x*sqrt(2))-1.
    function cdf(int256 x,int256 density) internal pure returns(int256){ unchecked {
        int256 y=ab(x);if(y>8*U)return x>0?U:int256(0);
        int256 n=35262496599891000;
        n=mul(n,y)+700383064443688000;n=mul(n,y)+6373962203531650000;
        n=mul(n,y)+33912866078383000000;n=mul(n,y)+112079291497871000000;
        n=mul(n,y)+221213596169931000000;n=mul(n,y)+220206867912376000000;
        int256 d=88388347648318400;
        d=mul(d,y)+1755667163182640000;d=mul(d,y)+16064177579207000000;
        d=mul(d,y)+86780732202946100000;d=mul(d,y)+296564248779674000000;
        d=mul(d,y)+637333633378831000000;d=mul(d,y)+793826512519948000000;
        d=mul(d,y)+440413735824752000000;
        int256 tail=mul(mul(density,2506628274631000200),divi(n,d));return x>0?U-tail:tail;
    } }
    function trunc(int256 m,int256 v,int256 lo,int256 hi) internal pure returns(int256 Z,int256 mt,int256 vt){ unchecked {
        if(v<=0)return (lo<=m&&m<=hi?U:int256(0),m,0);
        int256 sd=root(v);int256 a=divi(lo-m,sd);int256 b=divi(hi-m,sd);
        int256 pa=pdf(a);int256 pb=pdf(b);
        Z=cdf(b,pb)-cdf(a,pa);
        if(Z<1e6)return(Z,m<lo?lo:hi,v/4);
        int256 r=divi(pa-pb,Z);
        mt=m+mul(sd,r);vt=mul(v,U+divi(mul(a,pa)-mul(b,pb),Z)-mul(r,r));if(vt<0)vt=0;
    } }
    // ---- qm-spline lookup (QMS1 blob sha256 3ac7cb88..., 10,167 B): 5 cubic tensor B-splines over (row, column, sd level),
    // ask side only; bid = point mirror. Coefficients int16 (1/8 bps) as PUSH32 immediates, 16 lanes of (c+32768) per word.
    function cw0(uint256 i) internal pure returns(uint256){ unchecked { if(i<8){if(i<4){if(i<2){if(i<1){return 0x946594cb947894aa80009489986280009852988098639846984798398000983e;}return 0x800087468e9780008e0e8f578ec98e158e788e1f80008e5094a4800094f3941c;}if(i<3){return 0x85468606840d83bd83d783a0800083ba873d800087b1869b872f878f8732876a;}return 0x81d58254800082018339800083ee82eb852d826f82a5826f8000828185cd8000;}if(i<6){if(i<5){return 0x81d9800080ac835583a5821481f381b5800081cc859b800086c7835882588326;}return 0x830881b581c4817880008197835d800083aa82f881cc8294819581ea800081b2;}if(i<7){return 0x800080fa81bc8000817382a281c282008133817680008162831380008331826f;}return 0x80c480e780e27fab817e7e178000816b81ed80008297818281ed809481258205;}if(i<12){if(i<10){if(i<9){return 0x7fd67f03800081ea80848000808a80737fcf801e802d812580007d4180f88000;}return 0x80008000800c7fee80147ff4800a800e80007db2801f800080207ff97fdf7faf;}if(i<11){return 0x80027ffe80017ffb80007fc27ffd80007ffe80037ffd7ffb80087fc38000804d;}return 0x800080007fff8000800080007fff800080008000800080018001800080027ffe;}if(i<14){if(i<13){return 0x8000800080008000800080008000800080008000800080008000800080008000;}return 0x8000800080008000800080008000800080008000800080008000800080008000;}if(i<15){return 0x80008000800080008000800080008000800080007fff80008000800080008000;}return 0x9158964b93b0958980009481985a800097db98ac994497aa987297c680009836; } }

        int256 lv0=mul(mul(cl(Fv[0]),U-f)+mul(cl(Fv[2]),f),U-g)+mul(mul(cl(Fv[1]),U-f)+mul(cl(Fv[3]),f),g);
        int256 lv1=mul(mul(cl(Fv[4]),U-f)+mul(cl(Fv[6]),f),U-g)+mul(mul(cl(Fv[5]),U-f)+mul(cl(Fv[7]),f),g);
        return mul(lv0,U-tt)+mul(lv1,tt);
    } }
    function w2l(uint256 L) internal pure returns(int256){ unchecked {
        uint256 K=L<16?0x7ff77ff67ff57ff47ff27fef7fec7fe77fe27fd87fce7fc47fb07f9c7f7e7f60:(L<32?0x800780068005800480038002800180007fff7ffe7ffd7ffc7ffb7ffa7ff97ff8:(L<48?0x808280648050803c80328028801e801980148011800e800c800b800a80098008:0x00000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000080a0));
        return int256((K>>(16*(L&15)))&0xffff)-32768;
    } }
    // real.py/evalpol _pos2 over pol_mid's W2L (grid units of 5 bps), WAD in and out
    function pos2(int256 v) internal pure returns(int256){ unchecked {
        if(v<=-160*U)return 0; if(v>=160*U)return 48*U;
        uint256 lo=0;uint256 hi=48;
        while(hi-lo>1){uint256 md=(lo+hi)>>1;if(w2l(md)*U<=v)lo=md;else hi=md;}
        int256 a=w2l(lo);return int256(lo)*U+(v-a*U)/(w2l(hi)-a);
    } }
    function sdl(uint256 k) internal pure returns(int256){ unchecked { return int256((0x221a14100c080400>>(8*k))&0xff); } }
    // qm fee rule: w, w2 offsets (WAD bps), phase, synced flag, belief variance v (WAD, ln-price^2)
    function fees(int256 w,int256 w2,uint256 ph,bool syn,int256 v) internal pure returns(int256 fb,int256 fa){ unchecked {
        int256 sd=root(v)*10000;uint256 k;
        while(k<6&&sd>=sdl(k+1)*U)k++;
        int256 tt=clip((sd-sdl(k)*U)/(sdl(k+1)-sdl(k)),0,U);
        int256 pw=clip(w/5+160*U,0,320*U);int256 wq=(pw-160*U)*5;
        uint256 tb;int256 p2;int256 nc1;
        if(ph==0){tb=0;p2=clip(w2/5,-6*U,6*U)+6*U;nc1=12;}
        else{tb=(ph==1?1:3)+(syn?0:1);p2=pos2(w2/5);nc1=48;}
        int256 xa=surf(tb,pw,p2,k,tt)+wq-w;
        int256 xb=surf(tb,320*U-pw,nc1*U-p2,k,tt)+w-wq;
        fb=xb>0?U-exp(-xb/10000):int256(0);fa=xa>0?U-exp(-xa/10000):int256(0);
        fb=clip(fb,0,U/10);fa=clip(fa,0,U/10);
    } }
    function afterInitialize(uint256 x,uint256 y) external override returns(uint256,uint256){ unchecked {
        int256 sp=int256(y*1e18/x);
        slots[0]=uint256(uint128(int128(ln(sp))));
        slots[1]=uint256(uint128(int128(sp)))*(1+(uint256(1)<<128));
        slots[2]=2823606104386589*(1+(uint256(1)<<64));
        return(2823606104386589,2823606104386589);
    } }
    // filter update over a gap of dt steps; returns new m, v, rival spot r and the arb flag
    function update(int256 m,int256 v,int256 fb,int256 fa,int256 sp,int256 r,int256 s,bool buy,uint256 dt) internal pure returns(int256,int256,int256,bool arb){ unchecked {
        int256 lo=ln(mul(sp,U-fb));int256 hi=ln(divi(sp,U-fa));
        uint256 n=dt-1;if(n>12)n=12;
        for(uint256 i=0;i<n;i++){v+=893025000000;(,m,v)=trunc(m,v,lo,hi);}
        v+=893025000000;

        int256 sd=root(v);int256 la=divi(pdf(divi(lp-m,sd)),sd);
        (int256 Z,int256 mt,int256 vt)=trunc(m,v,lo,hi);
        int256 d=ab(ln(divi(s,sp)));if(d<1e9)d=1e9;
        int256 pi=pdf(divi(ln(d)+6801595083153746944,1176000000000000000));
        int256 lr=divi(mul(mul(Z,260000000000000000),pi),mul(d,1176000000000000000));
        pi=la+lr>0?divi(la,la+lr):int256(0);arb=pi>U/2;
        if(pi>5e15&&pi<995e15){
            m=mul(pi,lp)+mul(U-pi,mt);
            v=mul(pi,mul(lp-m,lp-m))+mul(U-pi,vt+mul(mt-m,mt-m));
        }else if(arb){m=lp;v=0;}else{m=mt;v=vt;}
        int256 pe=exp(m);r=clip(r,mul(pe,997e15),divi(pe,997e15));
        return(m,v,r,arb);
    } }
    function afterSwap(TradeInfo calldata t) external override returns(uint256,uint256){ unchecked {
        uint256 s0=slots[0];uint256 s1=slots[1];uint256 s2=slots[2];
        int256 m=int256(int128(uint128(s0)));int256 v=int256(int128(uint128(s0>>128)));
        int256 sp=int256(int128(uint128(s1)));int256 r=int256(int128(uint128(s1>>128)));
        int256 fb=int256(s2&M64);int256 fa=int256(s2>>64&M64);uint256 cnt=s2>>192&0xffffffff;bool syn=s2>>255==1;
        int256 s=int256(t.reserveY*1e18/t.reserveX);bool arb;
        if(t.timestamp>(s2>>128&M64)){(m,v,r,arb)=update(m,v,fb,fa,sp,r,s,t.isBuy,t.timestamp-(s2>>128&M64));cnt=0;syn=false;}
        uint256 ph;
        if(!arb){
            int256 c=t.isBuy?divi(mul(s,U-fb),997e15):divi(mul(s,997e15),U-fa);
            if(t.isBuy?c<r:c>r){r=c;syn=true;}

        int256 w=(ln(s)-m)*10000;int256 rr=(ln(r)-m)*10000;
        (fb,fa)=fees(w,rr,ph,syn,v);
        slots[0]=uint256(uint128(int128(m)))|uint256(uint128(int128(v)))<<128;
        slots[1]=uint256(uint128(int128(s)))|uint256(uint128(int128(r)))<<128;
        slots[2]=uint256(fb)|uint256(fa)<<64|t.timestamp<<128|cnt<<192|(syn?uint256(1)<<255:0);
        return(uint256(fb),uint256(fa));
    } }
}
```

### 1.3 The gate-F reference for qt1 (`qmref.py`)

The reference is standard-library Python: trim-2's filter (port-3's `standalone.Coarse` verbatim, plus `real.py`'s `synced` flag) and `real.py`'s `RealPolicy.lookup` qm rule over the tables decoded from the 10,167-byte QMS1 blob (sha256 `3ac7cb8811ecfb6a17f499aa4e9b70dd55f7fb6432b3aec3b904e11a3dece38e`, in the qm-spline artifact). Its pure-Python decoder matches qm-spline's numpy decoder exactly (max diff 0 over all ten tables; decoded JSON sha256 `4d97c205783ddff731fecd9dbdaea09c295954d2d2e96fbf25eec1320a5c22fa`), and it reproduces qm-spline's check values 443.101741 / 571.454483 / 525.908441 on seeds 10000..10002. Gate F replayed `replica2.run(seed, QMRef)` for seeds 70000..70049, the first 2,000 own-pool callbacks each, on a fresh pyrevm deployment at 245,000 gas per call: 100,050 calls succeeded, max |fee diff| 5.826e-06 bps.

```python
"""qt1 reference: Taylor's (gtmcknight) Gaussian filter (as port-3's standalone.Coarse / trim-2) + real.py's qm fee
rule over the DECODED qm-spline tables (QMS1 blob, sha256 3ac7cb88...). Standard library only.
usage: from qmref import QMRef; QMRef('blob.bin') is a replica2 policy (wants_j).
Init fees = real.py's init: the full plain pol_mid table at (0,0,0) = 0.002823606104386589 each.
"""
import math, struct

SIG2 = .000945 ** 2
LD_M, LD_S = math.log(11.12e-4), 1.176
INIT = 0.002823606104386589
MAXF = 0.1


def phi(x): return math.exp(-.5 * x * x) / 2.5066282746310002
def Phi(x): return .5 * (1 + math.erf(x / 1.4142135623730951))


def trunc(m, v, lo, hi):
    if v <= 0: return float(lo <= m <= hi), m, 0.
    sd = math.sqrt(v); a = (lo - m) / sd; b = (hi - m) / sd; z = Phi(b) - Phi(a)
    if z < 1e-12: return z, lo if m < lo else hi, v * .25
    pa, pb = phi(a), phi(b); r = (pa - pb) / z
    return z, m + sd * r, max(0, v * (1 + (a * pa - b * pb) / z - r * r))


def parse(blob):
    o = [0]
    def rd(fmt):
        v = struct.unpack_from('<' + fmt, blob, o[0]); o[0] += struct.calcsize('<' + fmt); return v
    assert blob[:4] == b'QMS1'; o[0] = 4
    form, ntab, nw, w0, h, ns = rd('BBHHBB'); assert form == 3
    S = list(rd('%dB' % ns)); n2 = rd('B')[0]; W2L = list(rd('%dh' % n2)); fb = rd('B')[0]
    tabs = []
    for _ in range(ntab):
        nr, nc, nk = rd('BBB')
        kr = list(rd('%dH' % (nr - 4))); kc = list(rd('%dH' % (nc - 4))); ks = list(rd('%dH' % (nk - 4)))
        assert nk == 4 and not ks
        tabs.append([nr, nc, nk, kr, kc])
    for t in tabs:
        t.append(list(rd('%dh' % (t[0] * t[1] * t[2]))))
    assert o[0] == len(blob)
    return dict(NW=nw, W0=w0, H=float(h), S=[float(s) for s in S], W2L=[float(v) for v in W2L], FB=fb, tabs=tabs)


def basis(knots, x):
    """all cubic B-spline basis values at x (Cox-de Boor recursion), right end included"""
    t = knots; n = len(t) - 4
    B = [1.0 if t[m] <= x < t[m + 1] else 0.0 for m in range(len(t) - 1)]
    if x >= t[-1]:
        last = max(m for m in range(len(t) - 1) if t[m] < t[m + 1]); B = [0.0] * (len(t) - 1); B[last] = 1.0
    for d in range(1, 4):
        Bn = [0.0] * (len(t) - 1 - d)
        for m in range(len(t) - 1 - d):
            a = t[m + d] - t[m]; b = t[m + d + 1] - t[m + 1]
            if a > 0: Bn[m] += (x - t[m]) / a * B[m]
            if b > 0: Bn[m] += (t[m + d + 1] - x) / b * B[m + 1]
        B = Bn
    return B[:n]


def surfaces(P):
    """F[t][level][row][col] = max(0, spline) at the grid nodes, in bps"""
    out = []
    for ti, (nr, nc, nk, kr, kc, C) in enumerate(P['tabs']):
        ncol = 2 * P['FB'] + 1 if ti == 0 else len(P['W2L'])
        Kr = [0.0] * 4 + [v / 64 for v in kr] + [P['NW'] - 1.0] * 4
        Kc = [0.0] * 4 + [v / 64 for v in kc] + [ncol - 1.0] * 4
        Ks = [0.0] * 4 + [len(P['S']) - 1.0] * 4
        Br = [basis(Kr, i) for i in range(P['NW'])]; Bc = [basis(Kc, j) for j in range(ncol)]
        Bs = [basis(Ks, l) for l in range(len(P['S']))]
        F = []
        for l in range(len(P['S'])):
            D = [[sum(Bs[l][s] * C[(s * nr + r) * nc + c] for s in range(nk)) / 8.0 for c in range(nc)] for r in range(nr)]
            E = [[sum(D[r][c] * Bc[j][c] for c in range(nc)) for j in range(ncol)] for r in range(nr)]
            F.append([[max(0.0, sum(Br[i][r] * E[r][j] for r in range(nr))) for j in range(ncol)] for i in range(P['NW'])])
        out.append(F)
    return out


class Tables:
    """A/B exactly as qms_decode.to_qm writes them (rounded to 6 decimals)"""
    def __init__(self, blob):
        P = parse(blob); self.P = P
        NW = P['NW']; w = [(i - P['W0']) * P['H'] for i in range(NW)]
        self.A = {}; self.B = {}
        for tag, F in zip(['0c', '1s', '1c', '2s', '2c'], surfaces(P)):
            A = [[[round(F[l][i][j] + w[i], 6) for j in range(len(F[l][i]))] for i in range(NW)] for l in range(len(F))]
            self.A[tag] = A
            self.B[tag] = [[row[::-1] for row in A[l][::-1]] for l in range(len(A))]


class QMRef:
    wants_j = True
    _cache = {}
    def __init__(self, blob_path):
        if blob_path not in QMRef._cache: QMRef._cache[blob_path] = Tables(open(blob_path, 'rb').read())
        self.T = QMRef._cache[blob_path]; P = self.T.P
        self.S = P['S']; self.W0 = P['W0']; self.NW = P['NW']; self.h = P['H']; self.FB = P['FB']; self.W2L = P['W2L']
        self.m = math.log(100); self.v = 0.; self.tlast = 0; self.cnt = 0; self.s2h = 100.; self.fb = self.fa = .003
        self.sp = 100.; self.synced = False
    def _pos2(self, v):
        W = self.W2L; n = len(W)
        if v <= W[0]: return 0.0
        if v >= W[n - 1]: return float(n - 1)
        lo, hi = 0, n - 1
        while hi - lo > 1:
            mid = (lo + hi) // 2
            if W[mid] <= v: lo = mid
            else: hi = mid
        return lo + (v - W[lo]) / (W[hi] - W[lo])
    def lookup(self, w, w2, phs, sd):          # real.py RealPolicy.lookup
        S = self.S; k = 0
        while k < len(S) - 2 and sd >= S[k + 1]: k += 1
        tt = min(1.0, max(0.0, (sd - S[k]) / (S[k + 1] - S[k])))
        tag = '0c' if phs == 0 else (str(phs) + ('s' if self.synced else 'c'))
        A, B = self.T.A[tag], self.T.B[tag]
        pw = min(self.NW - 1.0, max(0.0, w / self.h + self.W0))
        l2 = w2 / self.h
        if phs == 0:
            l2 = min(self.FB, max(-self.FB, l2)); p2 = l2 + self.FB; n2 = 2 * self.FB + 1
        else:
            p2 = self._pos2(l2); n2 = len(self.W2L)
        i = min(int(pw), self.NW - 2); j = min(int(p2), n2 - 2); f = pw - i; g = p2 - j
        def bl(Tb):
            return (Tb[i][j] * (1 - f) + Tb[i + 1][j] * f) * (1 - g) + (Tb[i][j + 1] * (1 - f) + Tb[i + 1][j + 1] * f) * g
        a = bl(A[k]) * (1 - tt) + bl(A[k + 1]) * tt
        b = bl(B[k]) * (1 - tt) + bl(B[k + 1]) * tt
        fa = 1.0 - math.exp(-(a - w) * 1e-4) if a > w else 0.0
        fb = 1.0 - math.exp(-(b + w) * 1e-4) if b > -w else 0.0
        return fb, fa
    def init(self, *args):
        self.fb = self.fa = INIT; return INIT, INIT
    def on_trade(self, is_buy, ax, ay, t, x, y, arb=False, p=100., s2=100., j=0):
        s = y / x; dt = t - self.tlast; is_arb = False
        if dt >= 1:
            self.cnt = 0; lo = math.log(self.sp * (1 - self.fb)); hi = math.log(self.sp / (1 - self.fa)); m, v = self.m, self.v
            for _ in range(min(dt - 1, 12)):
                v += SIG2; _, m, v = trunc(m, v, lo, hi)
            v += SIG2
            lp = math.log(s * (1 - self.fb)) if is_buy else math.log(s / (1 - self.fa)); sd = math.sqrt(v)
            la = phi((lp - m) / sd) / sd; Z, mt, vt = trunc(m, v, lo, hi); d = max(abs(math.log(s / self.sp)), 1e-9)
            lr = Z * .26 * phi((math.log(d) - LD_M) / LD_S) / (d * LD_S)
            pi = la / (la + lr) if la + lr > 0 else 0.; is_arb = pi > .5
            if .005 < pi < .995:
                m2 = pi * lp + (1 - pi) * mt; self.m, self.v = m2, pi * (lp - m2) ** 2 + (1 - pi) * (vt + (mt - m2) ** 2)
            elif is_arb: self.m, self.v = lp, 0.
            else: self.m, self.v = mt, vt
            pe = math.exp(self.m); self.s2h = max(pe * .997, min(pe / .997, self.s2h)); self.synced = False
        if not is_arb:
            cand = s * (1 - self.fb) / .997 if is_buy else s * .997 / (1 - self.fa)
            if (cand < self.s2h) if is_buy else (cand > self.s2h): self.s2h = cand; self.synced = True
            self.cnt += 1; ph = 1 if self.cnt == 1 else 2
        else: ph = 0
        self.tlast = t; self.sp = s
        fb, fa = self.lookup((math.log(s) - self.m) * 1e4, (math.log(self.s2h) - self.m) * 1e4, ph, math.sqrt(self.v) * 1e4)
        self.fb, self.fa = min(MAXF, max(0.0, fb)), min(MAXF, max(0.0, fa))
        return fb, fa
```

## 2. The qm policy's 1,792-seed confirmation (qm-2) and why qm-2 itself cannot ship

qm-2 (r4-qm-port copy 2; `TaylorGaussianQmSpline`, source sha256 `50a741b97a7ed79237ecbd34a4bc20b5c70b7872d8916f31dc3fe3f72b4fe859`, runtime 19,346 bytes, the Solidity block under "## Strategy.sol" of artifact `e50ab7b9…`) is the first qm port: trim-1's filter and math, the qm-spline tables as 306 PUSH32 words, Cox-de Boor bases at runtime. Gate P pass, gate F 5.83e-6 bps, gate Q inherited from qm-spline (tables unchanged). On its own 128 seeds (9534000..9534127) it scored +2.137 se 0.113 over t03 (124/128 wins) and +2.912 over IB with an engine peak of 245,140 and 0 OutOfGas. The requester asked for its 2,048-seed confirmation against trim-1 and, in parallel, for gas trims that keep its fees (notes 6 and 7).

### 2.2 Gas verdict on qm-2

qm-2 fails the goal's limits as shipped: a successful-call peak of 249,895 (4,895 over) and 33 OutOfGas callbacks across the seven blocks, with at least one OutOfGas in every block. Its 128-seed run had looked just over the line (245,140, 0 OOG); 1,792 seeds found the tail. The engine evidently lets some calls above the printed 245,000 succeed (net-1 at 245,377 and qm-2 at 249,895 both returned), but the goal's rule is the number and the OutOfGas count, and qm-2 meets neither. The engine's chunk counters cannot name the failing seeds; the scores above include whatever those failures cost qm-2.

| **qtr1** (r6-qm-trim copy 1, `TaylorGaussianQmTrimQtr1`) | trim-1 shell, 8 slots | 20,923 | bit-identical to qm-2 (same digest `5da30a88…`, 0 differing) | 5.83e-6 (inherited) | 180,421 | 228,156 / 0 (9537000..9537127) | +0.851 se 0.050 vs trim-1 (no t03 arm) | `f6717eba62e8164b32ca87ca0a718bb8888860da54b0fd3bc8830fcf5a73edf6` (44,942 B, recomputed) | `09741ad7…` |
| qm-1 (r4-qm-port copy 1, `TaylorGaussianQMSpline`, Q23 bases) | trim-1 shell | 20,135 | own fixed point | 9.9e-4 | 186,205 | 229,132 / 0 (9533000..9533127) | +2.207 se 0.096 vs t03; +2.975 se 0.112 vs IB | `c96e646d5c76ebcdf1e57aecbfe207b3a0e92e71281ac437eeb3046babb94883` | `e631c005…` |
| qtr4 (r7-qm-trim copy 4, `TaylorGaussianQmSplineG`) | trim-1 shell | 19,332 | bit-identical to qm-2 | 5.83e-6 | 214,730 | **249,129 / 2** (9540000..9540127): fails | 2 OOG, not scored | `ac5ff1b1…d5e1` | `dbb0431d…` |

What the trims changed (fees untouched in every case): qtr2 scalarised the eight node sums without changing accumulation or division order, shared the mirrored knot geometry while re-running the original Cox-de Boor recurrence in its original rounding order (reversing rounded weights would not be identical), and packed eight storage slots into four, each read once; qtr1 used binary knot search, six-knot windows and unrolled row/column evaluation with aligned coefficient words; qtr4 only changed the knot comparison and saved nothing. qt1 is a different shell: trim-2's byte-identical-to-net-1 filter plus a scalar/fixed-index spline contraction and a 20-function binary-tree dispatch over the 306 coefficient words (a single 306-leaf tree segfaulted solc at the default stack).

Because qtr1 and qtr2 return exactly qm-2's bytes on every replayed callback, qm-2's 1,792-seed confirmation is their confirmation (the engine is deterministic given the fees), minus only the OutOfGas callbacks qm-2 suffered and they would not. qt1 carries the same tables and the same reference within 5.83e-6 bps but was never compared bit for bit with qm-2, so for qt1 the 1,792 seeds confirm the policy and its own 128 seeds plus the board confirm the contract. Expected scores of qt1, qtr1 and qtr2 are therefore the same to within the rounding noise; the choice between them is gas and size. qtr2 has the most headroom (191,661 on its block; qm-2's peak rose about 4,800 between its 128-seed block and its 1,792-seed campaign, so budget for that), qt1 is the one already on the board.

## 4. The compression table

Sign convention: loss = full-table policy minus compressed-table policy on Taylor's replica, paired by seed, so positive is worse; "choose" is seeds 60000..61023 (n=1,024) and "report" is 10000..12047 (n=2,048, scored once after the choice). The full plain tables are six arrays of 321 rows (w = -800..800 bps step 5) by 13 (phase 0) or 49 (phases 1 and 2, nonuniform W2L axis) = 71,262 values in a 780,061-byte JSON; B is the exact point mirror of A (`B[i][j] = A[320-i][nc-1-j]`, zero differences over all 71,262 cells), so only A need be stored. The full qm tables are 8 sd levels x 5 tags x 321 x (13 or 49) = 1,073,424 values in a 7,892,018-byte JSON, mirror-symmetric in all but one cell (tag 1c, level 6, i=160, j=24, off by 0.71 bps). The fee surface F = A - w is never negative and is exactly 0 in about 47 % of cells.

|---|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| sym-int8 (r1-compress-a) | plain | mirror + per-row int16 base + int8 residuals at 1 bps, 81 own knots | 10,024 | -0.0013 (0.0108) | -0.0086 (0.0078) | lossless in mean | no contract |
| rows-10bps (r1-compress-a) | plain | int16, rows every 10 bps, all columns | 71,484 | +0.0133 (0.0121) | +0.0164 (0.0095) | quality fine, far too big | no contract |

Lookup cost of the shipped qm-spline representation, measured in qm-1's instrumented contract at w = R = 0: one ask+bid lookup 72.9k to 82.3k gas depending on phase and sd (phase 0 72,890; 1s 82,153; 1c 74,802; 2s 82,321; 2c 73,321), including ABI dispatch and the table init. qt1 brought the two surfaces to about 35-43k each by contracting into stack and fixed-index memory instead of dynamic arrays; qtr2 took another 42k off qm-2's pyrevm peak. The lattice line (section 6) is where gas ran out, not here.

One qualification applies to every qm contract: at one callback (seed 70026, callback 1702) unmodified `real.py` returns a raw bid fee of 0.12000793 while storing and applying the capped 0.10 (replica2's `clampf`); every contract returns 0.10. Against the applied fees the max difference is 5.83e-6 bps; against the raw uncapped return it would be 200.08 bps at that single callback. The engine and the replica both apply the cap, so the applied-fee reading is the one that matters for scores, but a literal raw-return reading of gate F is not met.

## 6. Lines that did not fit or did not pay

**Lattice filter (Taylor's `latt.py`, +4.26 with qm on the replica).** lattice-2 ported it exactly (matches Taylor's Python to 1e-8 bps, runtime 20,992 bytes) and measured it on 20,000 replayed callbacks: mean 453,463 gas, peak 10,513,884, 64.5 % of callbacks over 245,000. Reductions (pyrevm peak / callbacks over 245k / replica cost vs the full lattice, n=48): 61 cells x 5 bps cap 30: 3,075,267 / 4,695 / -0.043; 31 x 10 cap 2: 335,145 / 116 / -0.086; 61 x 5 cap 1: 575,880 / 4,705 / -0.173; 31 x 10 cap 1: 258,576 / 15 / -0.182. The best reduction still exceeds the whole budget in pyrevm before the engine's roughly 15-50k overhead and before any table lookup, and most of the +4.26 is the qm tables (+1.75 of it on that probe), which qt1 already has. Unmeasured ideas from the probe: a 3-sigma kernel cut, a skip threshold, 21 cells x 10 bps, an unrolled loop, one sigma*sqrt(n) diffusion. Line stopped.

**Arb-or-retail call (README open item 3, worth up to 2.7 with the true flag; +3.72 with plain tables on the replica).** Three classifier ideas moved the replica by at most +0.05 on the report set: per-run sigma and order rate +0.0235 se 0.0083 (arb-2), a conditional router inverse +0.0493 se 0.0120 (arb-3), arrival-pattern features +0.011 se 0.009 (r6-arb/ar2); the first-trade error rate stays at about 16.6 %. One idea did pay: r6-arb/ar3 keeps the classifier and instead quotes against the step's whole posterior (arb point mass plus a 3-point Gauss-Hermite quadrature of the truncated retail Gaussian), averaging the per-node table quotes: **+0.5667 se 0.0182 on choose and +0.5662 se 0.0125 on the report set, 1,746 of 2,048 wins, worst seed -1.50**, about 15 % of the true-flag gap, at 2-4 table lookups per callback (the 2-lookup qs=0 variant keeps +0.49 on choose). It was measured with the plain tables only; whether it adds on top of the qm tables is untested, and nothing from this line was ported in this goal. Its complete `realpq.py` (sha256 `488ad8a8…`) is in the ar3 artifact.

**qm-net.** 3,076 bytes but loss +0.589; the training had not converged when time ran out. Dropped in favour of qm-spline.

## 10. What is missing or qualified

- **qa3** (qm-2 on 9613824..9614079) had not landed: the qm policy's confirmation is n=1,792, not 2,048. **pb3** (port-2), **qt2** (second qm port into trim-2's shell), **qtr3** (third trim) and **ar1** (size-to-gap classifier) were also still running; their results are not in this report.
- **trim-1's block 9608704..9608959** was never run: the item landed twice on non-Linux seats (the Linux-only wheel cannot run there). trim-1's own confirmation is n=1,792; its 14 blocks as a comparator total 3,584 seeds.
- **trim-2 was never confirmed on 2,048 seeds**: its confirmation batches were refused twice by the plane because the briefs asked for a command's printed output (the same refusal lost six round-3 and three round-5 batches and burned 7,168 seeds, listed in section 8).
- **No direct qt1 vs IB run, and no callback-level comparison between qt1 and qm-2/qtr2.** qt1 vs IB is given by offset; the 1,792-seed figures are transferred to qt1 through the shared reference, as section 1.1 says.
- **qm-2's confirmation scores include its 33 OutOfGas callbacks**, which the engine's chunk counters cannot attribute to seeds; they can only have lowered qm-2's numbers.
- **Gate F is met on applied fees**, with the one raw-return exception of section 5.
- **Gate Q for the qm contracts is inherited** from qm-spline's measurement (rerun once by qm-1 from its contract constants), not re-measured per contract; the decoded tables are byte-identical in every qm contract.
- **Lattice**: no contract fits; **qm-net**: failed; **arb classifier**: nothing ported.
- Engine peaks are observed maxima on the stated seeds, not bounds: qm-2's rose from 245,140 on 128 seeds to 249,895 on 1,792. qt1's 208,775 and qtr2's 191,661 are 128-seed figures.
- Several results had source links the plane could not re-check (named in the root merges); their measurements are the workers' own runs with per-seed CSVs, hashes and harnesses inside the results, and nothing here is independently certified.
- The goal's `+2.83 / +3.77 / +4.26 / t03 about +1.45` are replica-vs-HA figures and were not converted to engine numbers; the engine evidence is the paired differences above.

## 11. What the next run should do

1. **Make qtr2 the working shell.** It returns qm-2's fees bit for bit, has the lowest engine peak of the qm contracts (191,661 on 128 seeds, about 53k under the cap) and the smallest runtime among them (19,945 bytes). Before building on it, give it the confirmation this goal could not: two blocks of 1,024 fresh seeds (from 9615360) as 4 x 256 items each, arms qtr2, qt1, trim-1, t03, reporting per-seed CSV, paired n / mean / se / worst5, per-chunk peaks and OutOfGas. That also yields the only direct qt1-vs-qtr2 comparison. Keep every confirm brief free of any request for printed output; the accepted round-4 and round-6 confirm briefs are the model.
